title: Hof backup plan
description: hofctl backup's own deterministic plan contract (ADR 0006) - the backup-kind analogue of plan-v2, bound to the target's host key, installationId, generation, and release-lock digest, plus this run's own exact consistency set and destinations. Never activates plan-v2's own dormant backup.create action - this is a wholly separate document kind with its own fixed, typed operation whitelist (see the operations $def below), because a backup needs to express a consistency set, multiple required destinations, and evidence that plan-v2 never had to.

planId.description: sha256 of this plan's own inputs+target binding+consistencySet+destinations, deterministic - never includes a timestamp. A host-key change, a different generation, or a changed destination set all produce a different planId, exactly as plan-v2's own planId already works.

backupId.description: Deterministic, derived from this plan's own content - shared across every destination's own snapshot in this one run, so a partial-failure retry can recognize which destinations already have a snapshot under this exact id and which don't.

trigger.description: manual: hofctl backup run directly, requires the operator's own explicit --approve-plan-id, exactly like apply. scheduled: the systemd timer firing an already-applied backup policy - no fresh interactive approval, since the policy itself was already approved when it was applied.

executable.description: false when blockers is non-empty (drift detected, another operation already in progress, a stale/unreadable signed release or backup-tool-lock, ...) - the runner must refuse a plan that isn't executable, exactly like apply.

generation.description: The generation actually being backed up - read from the target's own committed state under the mutex, immediately before this plan is built.

backupToolLockDigest.description: The signed backup-tool-lock this plan was verified against - independent of releaseLockDigest above (ADR 0006's own point: a backup-tool build moves independently of the platform release).

consistencySet.description: Every volume this backup must snapshot together for a coherent restore - every enabled unit's own volume (from backup-inventory.json, see render-topology.mjs) PLUS every retainedServices volume (disabled-but-retained persistent services are explicitly in scope here, unlike a plain apply).

destinations.description: Resolved from services.yml's own backup.destinations at planning time - same local/s3 shape, copied here rather than $ref'd across files (this repo's own convention). All configured destinations are required for this operation's own overall success (ADR 0006) - a plan with zero destinations is never executable.

retained.description: true for a disabled-but-retained persistent service's own volume (state.retainedServices) - false for a normally-enabled unit's volume. Both are in scope for this consistency set; this flag is purely informational (evidence/diagnostics), never changes how the volume is snapshotted.

retention.description: Copied from services-v1alpha1.schema.json's own backup.retention shape (never $ref'd across files).

destination.description: Copied from services-v1alpha1.schema.json's own backup.destinations item shape (never $ref'd across files) - name is this installation's own unique destination identifier (services.yml's own contract test already refuses a duplicate name).

operation.description: The Backup Flow's own fixed, typed operation whitelist (ADR 0006) - no generic executor, matching ADR 0004's own decision. Dispatched in list order, under the shared execution mutex.

resource.description: The unit, the fixed staging-tree label, or the destination name this operation concerns, depending on action.

destination.description: Only for snapshot.create - which configured destination this operation targets. One snapshot.create operation per destination, all sharing the plan's own backupId.

condition.description: Only for readiness.wait - reuses plan-v2's own running/healthy vocabulary.
